reflection_text.18:
The $x$-dependent part of expected payment is, up to the $x$-free term $t(\theta)$,

$C_{x}(\theta,x)=x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)$

and with the two point support $x\in\{0,1\}$

$C(\theta,0)=t(\theta)$ , $C(\theta,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)$

so that up to $t$

$\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta,1)-C(\theta,0)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)\ge0$,

$\Delta(\theta)=0\iff\theta=1$, $p(1)>0$, $F>0$, and for $0\le\theta<1$

$C(\theta,1)>C(\theta,0)$.

Hence $x^{*}(\theta)=0$ is the unique strict minimiser for every $\theta<1$ and $x^{*}(1)$ is indifferent, $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$.  Put $w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0$ for $\theta<1$.  $F$ decreasing implies $w'(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0$ on the interior, so $w$ and hence

$\Delta(\theta)=p(1)w(\theta)$

is strictly decreasing in $\theta$ and $\Delta(\theta)\downarrow0$ as $\theta\uparrow1$.  In smooth notation

$\partial_{x}C(\theta,x)=w(\theta)\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]$,
$\partial_{\theta x}^{2}C(\theta,x)=\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]w'(\theta)<0$

whenever $p+ xp'>0$, i.e. $C$ has decreasing differences in $(\theta,x)$.  The incremental cost of a strict auditor is therefore decreasing in truthfulness; a higher type has a smaller refusal risk $1-\theta$ and a smaller penalty $F(\theta)$, so strictness becomes relatively cheaper with $\theta$.  The Spence-Mirrlees single crossing is reversed in sign, the usual monotone comparative static is $x^{*}(\theta)$ weakly non-decreasing in $\theta$ and in the binary parametrisation the best reply is essentially flat,

$x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$, $x^{*}(1)\in\{0,1\}$,

with the weak dominance $C(\theta,0)\le C(\theta,1)$ for all $\theta\in[0,1]$, strict for $\theta<1$.  Strictly speaking there is no interior interval on which an increase in $\theta$ is associated with a strict decrease in the optimal $x$; the strict monotone decreasing set $x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ is empty.  In weak terms the lenient auditor is the unique best response for every imperfectly truthful type, i.e. for all $\theta<1$, and on the discrete support $\{0,1\}$ the strict preference for leniency is the malpractice type $\theta=0$ with indifference only at the top $\theta=1$.

The split in the deliberation is between the strict statement that the monotone ordering is $x^{*}\uparrow$ in $\theta$ and therefore the naïve “more truthful $\to$ more lenient’’ sorting is empty, and the reading that the weak dominance $C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)$ for $\theta<1$ is phrased as a preference for leniency on the whole interior, which collapses to the top indifference $\theta=1$ in the conventional tie-breaking.  The key driver is $\Delta'(\theta)=p(1)[-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)]<0$, so the rent of leniency is decreasing in $\theta$ and vanishes only at $\theta=1$.  Unresolved is whether the question is asked for strict decreasing best replies, which is empty, or for the weak dominance region $\theta<1$, with the discrete manifestation $\theta=0$, the boundary indifference being $\theta=1$.

4.text:
Up to the $x$-free tax $t(\theta)$

$$
C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)=x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)=w(\theta)g(x),\qquad 
w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0,\;g(x)=xp(x)\ge 0,
$$

and on the binary support

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta),
$$

so that with $p(1)>0$, $F(\theta)>0$

$$
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)\ge 0,
\qquad \Delta(\theta)=0\iff\theta =1,
$$

and $\Delta(\theta)>0$ for every $\theta<1$.  In particular

$$
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)\quad 0\le \theta<1,\qquad 
C(1,0)=C(1,1),
$$

i.e. $x^{* }(\theta)=0$ is the unique strict minimiser for every
imperfectly truthful type and $x^{*}(1)$ is indifferent.  Hence up to the
trivial indifference at the top the best reply is the flat map

$$
x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0,\qquad 0\le\theta<1,
$$

and $C(\theta ,0)=C(\theta ,1)$ only at $\theta=1$.
Now

$$
\frac{d}{d\theta}\Delta(\theta)=p(1)\frac{d}{d\theta}
\Big[(1-\theta)F(\theta)\Big]
=p(1)\Big[-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)\Big]<0,
\qquad 0<\theta<1,
$$

because $F'<0$.  With $x_{1}>x_{0}$

$$
C(\theta_{2},x_{1})-C(\theta_{2},x_{0})
-C(\theta_{1},x_{1})+C(\theta_{1},x_{0})
=\big[w(\theta_{2})-w(\theta_{1})\big]\big[g(x_{1})-g(x_{0})\big]<0
$$

for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$, i.e.

$$
\frac{\partial^{2}C}{\partial\theta\partial x}
=\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]\frac{d}{d\theta}\big[(1-\theta)F(\theta)\big]<0
$$

on the normal case $p+xp'>0$.  The marginal cost of strictness
$C_{x}(\theta ,x)=w(\theta)[p(x)+xp'(x)]$ is strictly decreasing in
$\theta$.  The cost of a strict auditor is $(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)$ and
it is decreasing in truthfulness; a higher $\theta$ makes a strict
auditor relatively cheaper.  In the usual monotone language the best
reply is weakly increasing in $\theta$, $x^{*}(\theta_{2})\ge x^{*}(\theta_{1})$
for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$.

Hence in the strict monotone sense $x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$
for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ never occurs on the interior.  The strict
decreasing relation $x^{*}\downarrow$ is empty; the lenient auditor is
strictly dominant for every $\theta<1$ and disappears only at the
degenerate indifference $\theta=1$.  In weak terms the lenient auditor
is the unique optimum on the whole interior $0\le\theta<1$, i.e. on the
discrete $\{0,1\}$ support the strict preference for leniency is the
malpractice type $\theta=0$ with $x^{*}(0)=0$ and the perfectly truthful
type $\theta=1$ indifferent, $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$.  This is the familiar
reversal of the naive signalling story: more truthful firms are weakly
more willing to hire the stricter, revenue-deterring auditor. ∎

6.text:
Up to the $x$ free term $t(\theta )$ the $x$ part of the expected payment is

$$
\Pi(\theta ,x)= {\mathbb P}\{{\rm refusal}\mid\theta ,x\}\,
{\mathbb P}\{{\rm RS}\mid{\rm refusal},x\}F(\theta)
          =x(1-\theta )p(x)F(\theta)\ge 0 ,
$$

so that with $C(\theta ,x)=t(\theta )+\Pi(\theta ,x)$

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta ),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta )p(1)F(\theta) ,
$$

and, $t$ being $x$ free,

$$
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)
        =(1-\theta )p(1)F(\theta)\ge0 ,\qquad 
\Delta(\theta)=0\iff \theta =1,
$$

$p(1)>0,\;F(\theta)>0$.  Hence

$$
C(\theta ,1)>C(\theta ,0)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \theta<1,
\qquad C(1,1)=C(1,0),
$$

i.e. for every imperfectly truthful type the lenient auditor $x=0$
is the unique strict minimiser of $C(\theta ,\cdot)$ and
$x^{* }(\theta)=0$ on $0\le \theta<1$.  Put
$H(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0$.  Then up to $t(\theta )$

$$
C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)=H(\theta )\,g(x),\qquad 
g(x)=xp(x),
$$

and $H$ is strictly decreasing on $[0,1]$ because $1-\theta$ and $F$
are decreasing and $F>0$,

$$
\frac{d}{d\theta}H(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0,
\qquad 0<\theta <1 .
$$

Hence for $x_{1}>x_{0}$

$$
\Delta_{x}C(\theta)=H(\theta)\big[g(x_{1})-g(x_{0})\big]
$$

is strictly decreasing in $\theta$ and

$$
C_{\theta x}(\theta ,x)=\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]\frac{d}{d\theta}H(\theta)<0
$$

on the usual regular case $p(x)+xp'(x)>0$.  $C$ has decreasing
differences in $(\theta ,x)$; the incremental cost of going from a
lenient to a strict auditor

$$
\Delta(\theta)=p(1)H(\theta)
$$

is strictly decreasing in $\theta$ and $\Delta(\theta)\downarrow0$ as
$\theta\uparrow1$.  In the smooth language the marginal cost of
strictness
$C_{x}(\theta ,x)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]>0$ for
$\theta<1$ is strictly decreasing in $\theta$.  A higher $\theta$
therefore lowers the marginal cost of strictness and the monotone best
reply is weakly non–decreasing in $\theta$,
$x^{*}(\theta_{2})\ge x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$,
the familiar $\theta\uparrow\Rightarrow x^{*}\uparrow$ sorting.

In the binary parametrisation this is the degenerate pooling
$x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0$ on the whole interior $0\le\theta<1$, with the
trivial indifference $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at the perfectly truthful limit.
Strictly speaking the strict monotone relation

$$
\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\;\Longrightarrow\;x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})
$$

never obtains on $]0,1[$; the strict preference for leniency is
exhausted at the malpractice type and is weakened as $\theta$ rises.
Up to the usual tie–breaking the lenient auditor is the unique strict
best response for every $\theta<1$, i.e. on the discrete support
$\{0,1\}$ for the type $\theta=0$, and the comparison disappears only at
the top indifference point $\theta=1$.  In particular there is no
interior $\theta>0$ for which a strictly higher degree of truthfulness
strictly induces a strictly more lenient choice; the strict decreasing
region for $x^{*}(\cdot)$ is empty, the weak dominance region for
$x=0$ being the interior $\theta<1$.  This is the usual reversal of the
naïve ``more truthful $\to$ more lenient'' story. ∎

10.text:
The $x$ dependent part of the expected payment is up to the $x$ free
term $t(\theta)$

$$
L(\theta ,x)= {\rm Pr}\{refusal\}\,{\rm Pr}\{RS\mid refusal\}F(\theta )
          =x(1-\theta )p(x)F(\theta )\ge 0 ,
\qquad C(\theta ,x)=t(\theta )+L(\theta ,x) .
$$

On the two point support $x\in\{0,1\}$

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta )p(1)F(\theta),
$$

so that with the normalisation $p_{1}=p(1)>0,\;F(\theta )>0$,

$$
\Delta (\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=(1-\theta )p_{1}F(\theta)\ge 0,
\qquad \Delta (\theta)=0\iff \theta =1 .
$$

Hence

$$
C(\theta ,1)>C(\theta ,0)\iff\theta<1,\qquad 
C(1,1)=C(1,0),
$$

i.e. $x^{*}=0$ is the unique strict minimiser of $C(\theta,\cdot)$ for
every imperfectly truthful type and $x^{*}(1)$ is indeterminate.  Up to
$t(\theta)$ the best reply is

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=0,\qquad 0\le\theta<1,
$$

and flat on the interior.  Put $w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0$ on
$\theta<1$.  $w$ is the product of the two decreasing functions
$1-\theta$ and $F$, so that

$$
\frac{d}{d\theta}w(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0,
\qquad 0<\theta<1,
$$

and

$$
\frac{d}{d\theta}\Delta(\theta)=p_{1}\frac{d}{d\theta}w(\theta)<0
$$

on the interior.  In the smooth notation

$$
C_{x}(\theta ,x)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)\,[p(x)+xp'(x)]>0,
\qquad 
C_{\theta x}(\theta ,x)=\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]\,\frac{d}{d\theta}
w(\theta)<0,
$$

so that $C(\theta ,x)$ has decreasing differences in $(\theta ,x)$.
The incremental cost of a strict audit, $\Delta(\theta)=(1-\theta)
p_{1}F(\theta)$, is strictly decreasing in truthfulness and is washed
out in the limit $\theta\to1$.  The lenient auditor is therefore
strictly cheaper for every $\theta<1$ and the (weak) rent of leniency
is

$$
G(\theta)=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)>0,
\qquad G'(\theta)<0,
$$

i.e. the preference for leniency is strongest for the most opportunistic
types and is monotone eroded as $\theta$ rises.

In particular the monotone comparative static is the opposite of the
naïve signalling story: the marginal cost of strictness falls with
$\theta$ and the best reply $x^{*}(\theta)$ is weakly non-decreasing in
$\theta$, in fact constant

$$
x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0\;\;\hbox{on}\;\;[0,1),\qquad
x^{*}(1)\in\{0,1\},
$$

so that in the strict monotone sense $x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$
for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ never occurs on the interior.  Strictly
speaking the set on which a strictly higher $\theta$ strictly induces a
strictly more lenient auditor is empty, the best reply being the flat
lenient corner $x^{*}=0$ for every imperfectly truthful firm.  With the
customary weak ordering this is phrased as the unique strict optimum
$x^{*}=0$ for every $\theta<1$, i.e. on the admissible interior
$0\le\theta<1$, and on the discrete support $\{0,1\}$ the strict
preference for leniency is the malpractice type $\theta=0$ with
indifference $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at the top type $\theta=1$.  The conventional
statement that more truthful firms are weakly more willing to use the
stricter, reputation-deterring, auditor is the opposite monotone
sorting $x^{*}(\theta)\uparrow$ in $\theta$, the limit case being the
trivial indifference at $\theta=1$. ∎

\[

\[

\qquad0<\theta<1,
\]

\[
\Delta(\theta)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)
\]

is strictly decreasing in $\theta$ and $\Delta(\theta)\downarrow0$ as
$\theta\uparrow1$.  In the smooth notation, with the usual $g'(x)>0$,

\[
C_{x}(\theta ,x)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]>0,
\qquad 
C_{\theta x}(\theta ,x)=\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]
\big[-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)\big]<0
\]

on $\theta<1$, i.e. $C(\theta ,x)$ has decreasing differences in
$(\theta ,x)$.  The marginal expected cost of raising $x$,

\[
C_{x}(\theta ,x)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big],
\]

falls with $\theta$: a higher $\theta$ lowers the refusal probability
$1-\theta$ and the penalty $F(\theta)$, so the cost of a strict auditor
falls with truthfulness.  In the usual Spence–Mirrlees language the
single crossing is reversed and the monotone efficient sorting is

\[
x^{*}(\theta)\ {\rm weakly\ increasing\ in\ }\theta ,
\]

indeed

\[
x^{*}(\theta)=0\qquad\forall\;0\le\theta<1,\qquad
x^{*}(1)\in\{0,1\},\;C(1,0)=C(1,1),
\]

taken to be $x^{*}\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$.  In particular there is no

strict sense.  The strict monotone decreasing relation
$x^{*}\downarrow$ in $\theta$ is empty on the admissible support.
Weakly the lenient auditor is the unique strict minimiser for every
$\theta<1$ and the rent of leniency

\[
C(\theta,1)-C(\theta,0)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)>0
\]

is strongest for the least truthful types and vanishes only at the
knife edge $\theta=1$.  On the two point support $\{\theta=0,1\}$ this is

interior $\theta<1$, with strict dominance for $0\le\theta<1$ and

‘more truthful $\to$ more lenient’ story: ceteris paribus a more
truthful firm is weakly more willing to bear the refusal risk and the

The marginal cost of raising $x$,

$$C_{x}(\theta ,x)=w(\theta)\bigl[p(x)+xp'(x)\bigr]>0\quad\theta<1,$$

falls with truthfulness, so the usual monotone comparative static is

$$x^{*}(\theta)\ {\rm weakly\ non-decreasing\ in\ }\theta .$$

On the binary support this is the flat best reply

$$x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0\ {\rm on}\ [0,1),\qquad 
C(\theta,1)=C(\theta,0)\ {\rm at}\ \theta=1,$$

i.e. the lenient auditor is the unique strict minimiser for every
imperfectly truthful type and is weakly dominant for the truthful type.
In particular there is no pair $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ with
$x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ in the interior of the type
space: the strict monotone decreasing relation $x^{*}\downarrow$ in
$\theta$ is empty.  Up to the trivial indifference at the top this is
the statement that the weak preference for leniency is $C(\theta,0)\le
C(\theta,1)$ for every $0\le\theta<1$, and in the discrete
$\{0,1\}$ parametrisation the strict preference for the lenient
auditor is the malpractice type $\theta=0$, $x^{*}(0)=0$, with
$x^{*}(1)\in\{0,1\}$ and $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$.  This is the reversal of the
naive signalling story: a higher $\theta$ makes a strict auditor
relatively cheaper, $ \partial_{\theta x}^{2}C<0$, so the conventional
sorting is $x^{*}\uparrow$ in $\theta$.  If weak dominance is counted as
a preference for leniency the weak optimal set is the whole interior
$\theta<1$, the degenerate indifference being $\theta=1$. ∎

16.text:
Up to the $x$–free term $t(\theta)$ the expected $x$–dependent part of the
payment is

$$L(\theta ,x)={\rm Prob}\{refusal\}\times p(x)F(\theta)
           =x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)\ge 0  ,$$

so that on the two point support

$$C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta),$$

and

$$\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)\ge 0,
\qquad\Delta(\theta)=0\iff\theta =1,
$$

$p(1)>0$, $F(\theta)>0$.  Hence

$$C(\theta ,1)>C(\theta ,0)\quad\forall\;0\le\theta<1,\qquad 
C(1,1)=C(1,0),$$

i.e. $x^{* }(\theta)=0$ is the unique strict minimiser for every
$\theta<1$ and $x^{*}(1)$ is indifferent.  Writing
$w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0$,

$$C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)=w(\theta)g(x),\qquad g(x)=xp(x),$$

so that on $\{\theta<1\}$ the minimisation of $C$ is up to the strictly
positive scalar $w(\theta)$ independent of $\theta$.  Moreover

$$\frac{d}{d\theta}w(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0,
\qquad
\frac{\partial^{2}C}{\partial\theta\partial x}
   =\bigl[p(x)+xp'(x)\bigr]\frac{d}{d\theta}w(\theta)<0 ,$$

for the usual $p(x)+xp'(x)>0$.  The incremental cost of strictness

$$\Delta(\theta)=p(1)w(\theta)$$

is therefore strictly decreasing in $\theta$ and

$$\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta}\bigl[C(\theta ,x_{1})-
C(\theta ,x_{0})\bigr]
 =\bigl[x_{1}p(x_{1})-x_{0}p(x_{0})\bigr]\frac{d}{d\theta}w(\theta)<0,
 \qquad x_{1}>x_{0},$$

so that $C$ has decreasing differences in $(\theta ,x)$ and the
marginal cost of strictness $\partial C/\partial x=(1-\theta)F(\theta)
\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]$ falls with $\theta$.  In the monotone
comparative–statics language $x^{*}(\theta)$ is weakly non-decreasing
in $\theta$; in the present penalty-only specification it is in fact
flat at the corner,

$$x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0,\qquad0\le\theta<1,$$

with the degenerate indifference $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at the top type.
The rent of leniency $G(\theta)=C(\theta,1)-C(\theta,0)=
(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)$ is strictly decreasing in $\theta$ and
vanishes only at $\theta=1$.  In particular there is no interior
$\theta$ with

$$ \theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\;\Longrightarrow\;x^{*}(\theta_{2})<
x^{*}(\theta_{1}) $$

in the strict sense.  The strict monotone decreasing relation
$x^{*}(\cdot)\downarrow$ is empty on $[0,1]$; the weak dominance of the
lenient auditor is

$$C(\theta,0)\le C(\theta,1)\iff\theta\le1,$$

with strict inequality $C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)$ for every imperfectly
truthful type $\theta<1$.  On the discrete support $\{\theta=0,1\}$ this
is the usual statement $x^{*}(0)=0$ strictly and $x^{*}(1)$ indifferent,
$x^{*}(1)\in\{0,1\}$.  Up to the trivial indifference at the perfect
type the lenient auditor is the unique best reply on the whole interior
$0\le\theta<1$, i.e. on the whole malpractice region, and the
conventional ``more truthful $\to$ more lenient'' sorting is reversed.
If a strict preference for leniency is required the only strictly
dominated type is the malpractice type $\theta=0$, the indifference
point being the top $\theta=1$.  This is the formal reversal of the
text-book signalling sorting. ∎

17.text:
Up to the $x$ free term $t(\theta )$ the part of expected payment which is
controlled by the auditor choice is

\begin{equation*}
L(\theta ,x)=x(1-\theta )p(x)F(\theta ),\qquad 
C(\theta ,x)=t(\theta )+L(\theta ,x),
\end{equation*}
with ${\mathbb P}\{{\rm refusal}\mid\theta ,x\}=x(1-\theta )$ and
${\mathbb P}\{{\rm RS}\mid{\rm refusal}\}=p(x)$.  On the two point
support

\begin{equation*}
L(\theta ,0)=0,\qquad L(\theta ,1)=(1-\theta )p(1)F(\theta )\ge 0,
\end{equation*}
so that with the normalisation $t(\theta )$ dropped

\begin{equation*}
\Delta(\theta ): =C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=(1-\theta )p(1)F(\theta )\ge0,
\end{equation*}
$\Delta(\theta )=0\iff\theta =1$, $p(1)>0$, $F>0$.  Hence

\begin{equation*}
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)\iff\theta<1,\qquad 
C(\theta ,0)=C(\theta ,1)\iff\theta=1,
\end{equation*}
i.e. on the interior the lenient auditor $x=0$ is the unique strict
minimiser,

\begin{equation*}
x^{*}(\theta )=0\qquad 0\le\theta <1,\qquad 
x^{*}(1)\in\{0,1\},
\end{equation*}
and $L(\theta ,0)\equiv0$.  Put $w(\theta )=(1-\theta )F(\theta )>0$,
$w'(\theta )=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0$, and
$g(x)=xp(x)$.  Then, mod $t$,

\begin{equation*}
C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)=w(\theta)g(x),\qquad 
\frac{\partial^{2}C}{\partial\theta\partial x}
 =\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]w'(\theta)<0,
\end{equation*}
whenever $p(x)+xp'(x)>0$.  The marginal expected cost of strictness

\begin{equation*}
C_{x}(\theta ,x)=(1-\theta )F(\theta )\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]>0,
\end{equation*}
is strictly decreasing in $\theta $,

\begin{equation*}
\frac{d}{d\theta}\Delta(\theta)
 =p(1)\big[-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)\big]<0,\qquad0<\theta<1,
\end{equation*}
so that $C(\theta ,x)$ has decreasing differences in $(\theta ,x)$.
The incremental cost of a strict auditor
$\Delta(\theta)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)$ is strictly decreasing in
truthfulness and vanishes at the truthful limit.  In particular the
best reply is weakly non-decreasing in $\theta$,
$x^{*}(\theta_{2})\ge x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$,
and on the admissible two-point support it is the flat map
$x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$ with the knife edge indifference
$C(1,0)=C(1,1)$.

Hence in the strict monotone sense there is no interior pair
$\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ with $x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$;
the strict monotone decreasing relation $x^{*}(\cdot)\downarrow$ is
empty.  In weak terms the lenient auditor is the unique strict best
reply for every imperfectly truthful type,
$C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)$ iff $\theta<1$, and it is the conventional
statement that the lenient choice is strictly dominant on the whole
interior $0\le\theta<1$, i.e. on the binary support the malpractice
type $\theta=0$.  The only degenerate point at which the strict
premium disappears is the perfectly truthful limit $\theta=1$, where
$x^{*}$ is indifferent.  This is the usual reversal of the naive
signalling story: a higher $\theta$ makes a strict auditor relatively
cheaper, so the efficient sorting is $x^{*}(\theta)\uparrow$, not
$x^{*}(\theta)\downarrow$, and up to the trivial indifference at the
top the lenient auditor pools the whole interior. ∎

14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Up to the inessential $t(\theta)$ the part of expected payment that is under the firm’s control is

$C(\theta ,x)=x(1-\theta )p(x)F(\theta )$,

and on $\{0,1\}$

$C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta)$, $C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta )$.

Hence for every interior type

$\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)>0$,

$\Delta(1)=0$,

and

$\Delta(\theta_{2})-\Delta(\theta_{1})
 =p(1)\big[(1-\theta_{2})F(\theta_{2})-(1-\theta_{1})F(\theta_{1})\big]<0$
for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ because $(1-\theta)F(\theta)$ is the product of two
decreasing positive functions.  The expected penalty generated by a
refusal, $x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)$, is therefore strictly decreasing in
$\theta$, $ \partial^{2}C/\partial\theta\partial x<0$, and the incremental
cost of being strict,
$L(\theta)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)$, is strictly decreasing in
truthfulness and vanishes only at the truthful limit.

In particular $C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)$ for every $0\le\theta<1$ and
$C(1,0)=C(1,1)$.  The lenient auditor $x=0$ is the unique strict
minimiser of $C(\theta ,\cdot)$ on the whole interior of the type space
and the rent of strictness is $\Delta(\theta)>0$ there.  On the
admissible two-point support this is the (weak) best response
$x^{*}(\theta)=0$ for all $\theta<1$ with indifference at $\theta=1$.
In the discrete parametrisation $\theta\in\{0,1\}$ this is the
malpractice type $\theta=0$ with the strict preference $x^{*}(0)=0$ and
the truthful type $\theta=1$ indifferent.

Hence the lenient contract is the cost minimising choice for every
non-perfect type, and the preference for leniency is monotone in the
usual applied sense: as truthfulness rises the expected loss from a
refusal falls, $(1-\theta)F(\theta)\downarrow$, so the firm remains with
– indeed the advantage of – the lenient auditor all the way up to the
limit $\theta\to1$.  In the conventional phrasing “the firms that choose
a more lenient auditor’’ this is the interior region $0\le\theta<1$, and
on the stated discrete support it is the malpractice type $\theta=0$,
i.e. the whole set of imperfectly truthful firms.  With the usual
tie-break the preference is still for leniency at the top type, so the
effective comparative static is a weakly decreasing choice in
truthfulness on $[0,1)$, the only degenerate point being the perfect
truthfulness limit $\theta=1$ where the refusal probability
$x(1-\theta)$ is identically zero. ∎

12.text:
With the term $t(\theta)$ which is $x$ free write, up to the additive constant
$t(\theta)$,

$$
C_{x}(\theta ,x)=x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)=w(\theta)g(x) ,
\qquad w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0,\;\;g(x)=xp(x),
$$

$$
C(\theta ,x)=t(\theta)+w(\theta)g(x),\qquad 0\le x\le 1 .
$$

On the admissible two point set $x\in\{0,1\}$

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)
$$

and hence up to $t(\theta)$

$$
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)\ge 0,
\qquad \Delta(\theta)=0\iff\theta =1,
$$

$p(1)>0$, $F(\theta)>0$.  In particular

$$
C(\theta ,1)>C(\theta ,0)\iff\theta<1,\qquad 
C(1,1)=C(1,0)=t(1),
$$

so that for every non perfectly truthful type the $x$–dependent part of
expected payment is strictly minimised at the lenient corner

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=0,\qquad 0\le\theta<1,
$$

and $x^{*}(1)\in\{0,1\}$ is indifferent.  The rent of strictness is

$$
\Delta(\theta)=p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)=p(1)w(\theta) ,
$$

and $w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)$ is the product of two decreasing
functions, $w'(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0$ on the
interior, so that

$$
\Delta(\theta_{2})-\Delta(\theta_{1})
 =p(1)\Big[(1-\theta_{2})F(\theta_{2})-(1-\theta_{1})F(\theta_{1})\Big]<0,
\qquad \theta_{2}>\theta_{1},
$$

i.e. $\Delta(\theta)$ is strictly decreasing in $\theta$ and
$\Delta(\theta)\downarrow0$ as $\theta\uparrow1$.  In smooth notation

$$
C_{x}(\theta ,x)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big],\qquad
C_{\theta x}(\theta ,x)=\big[-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)\big]
\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]<0,
$$

on $\{p(x)+xp'(x)>0\}$, i.e. $C(\theta ,x)$ has decreasing differences
in $(\theta ,x)$ and the usual Spence-Mirrlees single crossing is
reversed.  The marginal expected cost of strictness falls with
$\theta$,

$$
\frac{d}{d\theta}\Delta(\theta)=p(1)\frac{d}{d\theta}
\big[(1-\theta)F(\theta)\big]<0,
$$

so a higher $\theta$ makes a strict auditor relatively cheaper.  Hence
the best reply is weakly non-decreasing in $\theta$ and on the binary
support it is in fact flat at the lenient corner,

$$
x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0\ {\rm on}\ [0,1),\qquad 
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)\ {\rm for}\ \theta<1,
$$

with the degenerate indifference $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at the top type.  In
the strict monotone sense $x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ for
$\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ never occurs on the interior: the strict
decrease set is empty.  Weakly the lenient auditor is the unique
cost minimiser for every imperfectly truthful type, i.e. for the whole
interior $0\le\theta<1$, and on the discrete support $\{0,1\}$ this is
the malpractice type $\theta=0$ with the top type $\theta=1$
indifferent.  This is the familiar reversal of the naive belief: more
truthful types are weakly less averse to strictness and the
perverse $x^{*}\downarrow$ sorting is obtained only at the degenerate
limit $\theta=1$ where the refusal risk $x(1-\theta)$ vanishes. ∎

$$

strictness
$C_{x}(\theta ,x)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]>0$ for

therefore lowers the marginal cost of strictness and the monotone best
reply is weakly non–decreasing in $\theta$,
$x^{*}(\theta_{2})\ge x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$,
the familiar $\theta\uparrow\Rightarrow x^{*}\uparrow$ sorting.

$$

$$
L(\theta ,x)= {\rm Pr}\{ {\rm refusal}\}{\rm Pr}\{RS\mid {\rm refusal}\}F(\theta )

$$

so that for the two admissible technologies

$$
L(\theta ,0)=0,\qquad 
L(\theta ,1)=(1-\theta )p(1)F(\theta)>0,
$$

and $L(1,1)=L(1,0)=0$ because the refusal probability $x(1-\theta)$ vanishes at the top.  Hence

$$
C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)= \Delta(\theta):=(1-\theta )p(1)F(\theta)\ge0,
$$

with $\Delta(\theta)>0$ iff $\theta<1$ and $\Delta(1)=0$.  $p(1)>0$ and $F(\theta)>0$, so the lenient auditor $x=0$ is the unique strict minimiser of $C(\theta,\cdot)$ for every non-perfect type and the two technologies are payoff equivalent only at the perfectly truthful limit.

$$
\Delta(\theta)=p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)
$$

is the expected penalty saved by avoiding a refusal.  $1-\theta$ and $F(\theta)$ are decreasing, hence $h(\theta):=(1-\theta)F(\theta)$ is strictly decreasing on $[0,1]$ and

$$
\Delta'(\theta)=p(1)\big[-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)\big]<0,
\qquad 0\le\theta<1,
$$

so the premium for being strict is eroded as truthfulness rises.  The incremental cost of strictness falls with $\theta$, $L(\theta,1)-L(\theta,0)\downarrow0$ as $\theta\uparrow1$, and the refusal risk $x(1-\theta)$ shrinks with $\theta$. $G(\theta)=C(\theta,1)-C(\theta,0)>0$, is monotone decreasing in truthfulness and is strictly positive on the whole interior of the type space.

Therefore on the admissible support the lenient auditor is strictly optimal for every imperfectly truthful firm and remains optimal – up to the indifference at the top – as $\theta$ increases.  In the binary parametrisation this is the interior region

$$
C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\iff (1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,
$$

$$

$$

C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta )p(1)F(\theta),
$$

so that with the normalisation $p_{1}=p(1)>0,\;F(\theta )>0$,

$$

\qquad \Delta (\theta)=0\iff \theta =1 .
$$

$$
C(\theta ,1)>C(\theta ,0)\iff\theta<1,\qquad 
C(1,1)=C(1,0),
$$

i.e. $x^{*}=0$ is the unique strict minimiser of $C(\theta,\cdot)$ for
every imperfectly truthful type and $x^{*}(1)$ is indeterminate.  Up to

$$

$$

$\theta<1$.  $w$ is the product of the two decreasing functions

$$
\frac{d}{d\theta}w(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0,
\qquad 0<\theta<1,
$$

and

$$
\frac{d}{d\theta}\Delta(\theta)=p_{1}\frac{d}{d\theta}w(\theta)<0
$$

on the interior.  In the smooth notation

$$
C_{x}(\theta ,x)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)\,[p(x)+xp'(x)]>0,
\qquad

w(\theta)<0,
$$

strictly cheaper for every $\theta<1$ and the (weak) rent of leniency

$$
G(\theta)=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)>0,
\qquad G'(\theta)<0,
$$

=: \Delta(\theta)\ge0,  $$
with $\Delta(\theta)>0$ iff $\theta<1$ and $\Delta(1)=0$.
Up to the irrelevant $t(\theta)$ the lenient auditor $x=0$ is the unique
strict minimiser of

$$G(\theta ,x)=x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)$$

on the whole interior of the type space.  On $\{0,1\}$

$$x^{*}(\theta)=0\iff \Delta(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,$$

and $x^{*}(1)$ is indifferent.  In particular

$$C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1),\qquad 0\le\theta<1, $$

so the expected penalty saved by avoiding a refusal is
$ \Delta(\theta)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)$.  Since $(1-\theta)$ and $F$
are decreasing, $w(\theta):=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0$ is strictly decreasing
on $[0,1)$ and

$$\frac{d}{d\theta}\Delta(\theta)=p(1)\big[-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)\big]<0,
\qquad 0<\theta<1, $$

i.e. the rent of the lenient auditor is strictly decreasing in
truthfulness and is washed out in the limit $w(\theta)\downarrow0$ as
$\theta\uparrow1$.  The incremental loss from a strict auditor is
therefore monotone in $\theta$; the more truthful the accounts the
smaller the exposure $1-\theta$ and the smaller the penalty loading
$F(\theta)$, so the (weak) incentive to stay with the low refusal-risk
technology $x=0$ is relaxed as $\theta$ rises and disappears only at the
degenerate truthful limit.

In the usual monotone language this is the familiar interior dominance
region.  Up to the indifference at the top the cost minimising choice is
$x^{*}\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$.  Hence every non-perfect type, and in the
two-point parametrisation the malpractice type $\theta=0$, strictly
prefers the lenient auditor and the preference for leniency is monotone
in $\theta$.  On the admissible support the weak preference for
leniency holds for the whole interior $0\le\theta<1$, i.e. effectively
$\theta<1$, with the limiting indifference $\theta=1$ where the refusal
probability $x(1-\theta)$ vanishes.  This is the interior
‘more truthful $\to$ more lenient’ pooling that the model delivers in
the absence of a separate benefit of strict auditing. ∎

$$L(\theta ,x) ={\rm Pr}\{ {\rm refusal}\}{\rm Pr}\{RS\mid {\rm refusal}\}

$$C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)$$
and with $p(1)>0,\;F(\theta)>0$

$$\Delta (\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)
      =(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)\ge0 ,
\qquad \Delta(\theta)=0\iff\theta=1 .$$

$$C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)\iff 0\le\theta<1,\qquad 
C(1,0)=C(1,1),$$

$$L(\theta ,0)=0<L(\theta ,1)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta),\qquad\theta<1.$$

In particular

$$x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,
\qquad0\le\theta<1,$$

and $x^{*}(1)$ is indifferent.  Put $w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0$,
$\theta<1$.  $F$ decreasing gives in the monotone sense

$$w(\theta_{2})-w(\theta_{1})=
-( \theta_{2}-\theta_{1})F(\theta_{2})
+(1-\theta_{1})\big[F(\theta_{2})-F(\theta_{1})\big]<0,
\qquad\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},$$

$$C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)=w(\theta)g(x)$$

-\Big[C(\theta_{1},x_{1})-C(\theta_{1},x_{0})\Big]
 =\big[w(\theta_{2})-w(\theta_{1})\big]\big[g(x_{1})-g(x_{0})\big]<0,
$$
for $x_{1}>x_{0}$.  Hence

$$\frac{\partial^{2}C}{\partial\theta\partial x}
 =\bigl[p(x)+xp'(x)\bigr]\big[-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)\big]<0
$$

on the interior, i.e. $C$ has decreasing differences in $(\theta ,x)$.
The incremental cost of strictness

$$\Delta(\theta)=p(1)w(\theta)=p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)$$

is strictly decreasing in $\theta$, $\Delta'(\theta)<0$ in the monotone

$$C_{x}(\theta ,x)=w(\theta)\bigl[p(x)+xp'(x)\bigr]>0\quad\theta<1,$$

falls with truthfulness, so the usual monotone comparative static is

imperfectly truthful type and is weakly dominant for the truthful type.

\begin{equation*}

C(\theta ,0)=C(\theta ,1)\iff\theta=1,
\end{equation*}
i.e. on the interior the lenient auditor $x=0$ is the unique strict

\begin{equation*}

\end{equation*}

$g(x)=xp(x)$.  Then, mod $t$,

\begin{equation*}

 =\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]w'(\theta)<0,
\end{equation*}
whenever $p(x)+xp'(x)>0$.  The marginal expected cost of strictness

\begin{equation*}
C_{x}(\theta ,x)=(1-\theta )F(\theta )\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]>0,
\end{equation*}

 =p(1)\big[-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)\big]<0,\qquad0<\theta<1,
\end{equation*}

$\Delta(\theta)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)$ is strictly decreasing in

best reply is weakly non-decreasing in $\theta$,

PUBLIC RESPONSE: Up to the $x$-free tax $t(\theta)$ the auditor controllable part of expected payment is

$$
L(\theta,x) ={\mathbb P}\{{\rm refusal}\mid\theta,x\}\,
{\mathbb P}\{{\rm RS}\mid{\rm refusal}\}F(\theta)
          =x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)\ge0 ,
\qquad C(\theta,x)=t(\theta)+L(\theta,x).
$$

On the admissible binary support $x\in\{0,1\}$

$$
C(\theta,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta),
$$

so that

$$
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta,1)-C(\theta,0)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)\ge0,
$$

$p(1)>0$, $F(\theta)>0$.  Hence

$$
C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\iff (1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,
\qquad C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1).
$$

The lenient technology $x=0$ is therefore the unique strict minimiser of $C(\theta,\cdot)$ for every imperfectly truthful type and the two technologies are payoff equivalent only at the degenerate limit $\theta=1$ where the refusal probability $x(1-\theta)$ vanishes.

Write $w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0$ for $\theta<1$.  $1-\theta$ and $F$ are decreasing, so $w$ is strictly decreasing in the monotone sense and

$$
\Delta(\theta)=p(1)w(\theta),\qquad 
\Delta(\theta_{2})-\Delta(\theta_{1})
 =p(1)\big[w(\theta_{2})-w(\theta_{1})\big]<0
$$
for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ on the interior.  The expected penalty saved by avoiding a refusal,
$G(\theta)=C(\theta,1)-C(\theta,0)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)$, is strictly positive on the whole interior and is monotone eroded as $\theta$ rises, $G(\theta)\downarrow0$ as $\theta\uparrow1$.

In particular

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta,x)=0,\qquad 0\le\theta<1,
$$

with $x^{*}(1)$ indifferent.  Up to the trivial indifference at the top the best reply is the flat map $x^{*}\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$.  The weak dominance of leniency is
$C(\theta,0)\le C(\theta,1)$ for every $\theta\le1$ with strict inequality for $\theta<1$.

That is the economically relevant set on which leniency is strictly optimal: the interior $0\le\theta<1$, i.e. $\theta<1$, and on the stated discrete support $\{\theta=0,1\}$ the strict preference for leniency is the malpractice type $\theta=0$ with the limiting indifference $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at $\theta=1$.

The claim that the strict monotone relation $x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ is empty is a statement about a strict comparative static and it uses the sign of
$C_{\theta x}=[p(x)+xp'(x)]w'(\theta)$.  The problem is explicitly stated with $t,p,F$ decreasing but not necessarily differentiable and with the implicit function theorem not applicable.  The sign of $p(x)+xp'(x)$ and the differentiability needed for the usual decreasing-differences argument are not guaranteed in the stated primitive monotone setting, so the sign reversal that is invoked for the empty strict monotone set cannot be asserted on the primitives alone.

In the level-set reading that the question asks for, the firms that actually choose the lenient auditor are precisely the imperfect types.  The rent of leniency is
$C(\theta,1)-C(\theta,0)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)>0$ for every $\theta<1$, largest for the least truthful firms and monotone decreasing to zero at the perfect truthfulness limit.  On the binary parametrisation this is the usual statement $x^{*}(0)=0$ strictly and $x^{*}(1)$ indifferent; i.e. the (weak) preference for leniency holds for the whole interior $\theta<1$.

$$

$$

Up to the $x$–free tax $t(\theta)$ the $x$–dependent part of expected
payment is

$$
L(\theta ,x)={\rm Pr}\{refusal\}{\rm Pr}\{RS\mid refusal\}F(\theta)
      =x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)\ge0 ,
\qquad 
C(\theta ,x)=t(\theta)+L(\theta ,x) ,
$$

and on the binary admissible set

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta),
$$

so that with $p_{1}=p(1)>0$, $F(\theta)>0$

\begin{equation*}
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)
        =(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)=p_{1}w(\theta),\qquad 
w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0,
\end{equation*}
is the $x$-rent of the lenient auditor.  $w(\theta)$ is the product of
the two decreasing maps $1-\theta$ and $F$ and hence

$$
w'(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0,\qquad
\Delta'(\theta)=p_{1}w'(\theta)<0,\qquad0<\theta<1,
$$
with $\Delta(\theta)\downarrow0$ as $\theta\uparrow1$ and
$\Delta(1)=0$.  In particular

$$
C(\theta ,1)>C(\theta ,0)\iff (1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)>0
\iff\theta<1 ,\qquad C(1,1)=C(1,0)=t(1),
$$

so that on the interior

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad0\le\theta<1,
$$

and $x^{*}(1)$ is indifferent.  With the usual regularity
$p(x)+xp'(x)>0$

$$
C_{x}(\theta ,x)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]>0,
\qquad 
C_{\theta x}(\theta ,x)=\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]w'(\theta)<0 ,
$$

i.e. $C(\theta ,x)$ has decreasing differences in $(\theta ,x)$.  The
marginal expected cost of strictness $C_{x}$ is strictly decreasing in
$\theta$ and the incremental cost of a strict auditor
$\Delta(\theta)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)$ is strictly decreasing in
truthfulness and is washed out at $\theta=1$.  Hence

$$
C(\theta_{2},x_{1})-C(\theta_{2},x_{0})
-\big[C(\theta_{1},x_{1})-C(\theta_{1},x_{0})\big]
 =\big[w(\theta_{2})-w(\theta_{1})\big]\big[g(x_{1})-g(x_{0})\big]<0,
\qquad\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},\;x_{1}>x_{0},
$$

with $g(x)=xp(x)$.  The best reply is therefore weakly non-decreasing
in $\theta$,

$$
x^{*}(\theta_{2})\ge x^{*}(\theta_{1})\quad{\rm for}\quad\theta_{2}>
\theta_{1},
$$

and on the binary support it is the flat pooling

$$
x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0\ {\rm on}\ [0,1),\qquad 
C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\ {\rm for}\ \theta<1,
$$
with the knife edge $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$.  In strict monotone terms

$$
\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\Longrightarrow x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})
$$

never occurs on $]0,1[$; the strict monotone decreasing set is empty.
The usual Spence–Mirrlees ordering is reversed: a higher $\theta$
makes a strict auditor relatively cheaper, $C_{\theta x}<0$, so the
conventional sorting is $x^{*}(\theta)\uparrow$ in $\theta$.

Weakly the lenient auditor is the unique strict cost minimiser for
every imperfectly truthful type,

$$
C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\iff\theta<1,
$$

i.e. $C(\theta,0)\le C(\theta,1)$ on the whole interior $[0,1)$ with
strict inequality for $\theta<1$ and the rent of leniency
$G(\theta)=\Delta(\theta)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)>0$ is strictly
decreasing in $\theta$ and vanishes only at $\theta=1$.  On the stated
two-point support $\{\theta=0,1\}$ this is the strict preference
$x^{*}(0)=0$ for the malpractice type and indifference
$C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at the perfectly truthful type, the weak dominance
region for leniency being the interior $\theta<1$, effectively the
malpractice type $\theta=0$.  This is the reversal of the naive
signalling story; up to the degenerate indifference at $\theta=1$ the
lenient auditor pools the whole interior. ∎

Up to the $x$-free tax $t(\theta)$ the auditor controllable part of expected payment is

$$
L(\theta,x) ={\mathbb P}\{{\rm refusal}\mid\theta,x\}\,
{\mathbb P}\{{\rm RS}\mid{\rm refusal}\}F(\theta)
          =x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)\ge0 ,
\qquad C(\theta,x)=t(\theta)+L(\theta,x).
$$

On the admissible binary support $x\in\{0,1\}$

$$
C(\theta,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta),
$$

so that

$$
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta,1)-C(\theta,0)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)\ge0,
$$

$p(1)>0$, $F(\theta)>0$.  Hence

$$
C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\iff (1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,
\qquad C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1).
$$

The lenient technology $x=0$ is therefore the unique strict minimiser of $C(\theta,\cdot)$ for every imperfectly truthful type and the two technologies are payoff equivalent only at the degenerate limit $\theta=1$ where the refusal probability $x(1-\theta)$ vanishes.

Write $w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0$ for $\theta<1$.  $1-\theta$ and $F$ are decreasing, so $w$ is strictly decreasing in the monotone sense and

$$
\Delta(\theta)=p(1)w(\theta),\qquad 
\Delta(\theta_{2})-\Delta(\theta_{1})
 =p(1)\big[w(\theta_{2})-w(\theta_{1})\big]<0
$$
for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ on the interior.  The expected penalty saved by avoiding a refusal,
$G(\theta)=C(\theta,1)-C(\theta,0)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)$, is strictly positive on the whole interior and is monotone eroded as $\theta$ rises, $G(\theta)\downarrow0$ as $\theta\uparrow1$.

In particular

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta,x)=0,\qquad 0\le\theta<1,
$$

with $x^{*}(1)$ indifferent.  Up to the trivial indifference at the top the best reply is the flat map $x^{*}\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$.  The weak dominance of leniency is
$C(\theta,0)\le C(\theta,1)$ for every $\theta\le1$ with strict inequality for $\theta<1$.

That is the economically relevant set on which leniency is strictly optimal: the interior $0\le\theta<1$, i.e. $\theta<1$, and on the stated discrete support $\{\theta=0,1\}$ the strict preference for leniency is the malpractice type $\theta=0$ with the limiting indifference $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at $\theta=1$.

The claim that the strict monotone relation $x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ is empty is a statement about a strict comparative static and it uses the sign of
$C_{\theta x}=[p(x)+xp'(x)]w'(\theta)$.  The problem is explicitly stated with $t,p,F$ decreasing but not necessarily differentiable and with the implicit function theorem not applicable.  The sign of $p(x)+xp'(x)$ and the differentiability needed for the usual decreasing-differences argument are not guaranteed in the stated primitive monotone setting, so the sign reversal that is invoked for the empty strict monotone set cannot be asserted on the primitives alone.

In the level-set reading that the question asks for, the firms that actually choose the lenient auditor are precisely the imperfect types.  The rent of leniency is
$C(\theta,1)-C(\theta,0)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)>0$ for every $\theta<1$, largest for the least truthful firms and monotone decreasing to zero at the perfect truthfulness limit.  On the binary parametrisation this is the usual statement $x^{*}(0)=0$ strictly and $x^{*}(1)$ indifferent; i.e. the (weak) preference for leniency holds for the whole interior $\theta<1$.

Up to the $x$-free tax $t(\theta)$ the part of the expected payment that is under the firm’s control is

$$
L(\theta,x)=\Pr\{refusal\}\,p(x)F(\theta)=x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)\ge 0,
\qquad C(\theta,x)=t(\theta)+L(\theta,x).
$$

On the admissible binary support

$$
C(\theta,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta),
$$

so that, with $p_{1}=p(1)>0$ and $F(\theta)>0$,

$$
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta,1)-C(\theta,0)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)\ge0,
\qquad \Delta(\theta)=0\iff\theta=1.
$$

Hence

$$
C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\iff\Delta(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,
\qquad C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1),
$$

i.e. the lenient technology $x=0$ is the unique strict minimiser of $C(\theta,\cdot)$ for every imperfectly truthful type and the two technologies are payoff equivalent only at the perfect-truth limit where the refusal probability $x(1-\theta)$ vanishes.

Write $w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0$ on $\theta<1$.  $1-\theta$ and $F$ are decreasing, so $w$ is strictly decreasing in the monotone sense and

$$
\Delta(\theta)=p_{1}w(\theta),\qquad 
\Delta(\theta_{2})-\Delta(\theta_{1})=p_{1}\big[w(\theta_{2})-w(\theta_{1})\big]<0,
\;\; \theta_{2}>\theta_{1},
$$

with $\Delta(\theta)\downarrow0$ as $\theta\uparrow1$.  The expected penalty saved by avoiding a refusal,
$G(\theta)=C(\theta,1)-C(\theta,0)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)$,
is therefore strictly positive on the interior and is monotone eroded as truthfulness rises.  In particular

$$
\frac{\partial^{2}C}{\partial\theta\partial x}
=[p(x)+xp'(x)]\frac{d}{d\theta}[(1-\theta)F(\theta)]<0
$$

on the interior, so the incremental cost of going from $x=0$ to $x=1$ is decreasing in $\theta$.  A higher $\theta$ lowers the exposure $1-\theta$ and the penalty loading $F(\theta)$, so the (weak) incentive to stay with the low refusal-risk technology $x=0$ is relaxed monotonically with $\theta$ but it remains strictly positive until the refusal risk is eliminated.

On $\{0,1\}$ this is

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=0\iff\Delta(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,
$$

with $x^{*}(1)$ indifferent.  In the usual applied phrasing the lenient auditor is the cost minimising choice for every non-perfect type, i.e. for the whole interior $0\le\theta<1$, and on the stated discrete support $\{\theta=0,1\}$ it is the malpractice type $\theta=0$ with the top type $\theta=1$ the degenerate indifference boundary $\Delta(1)=0$.

In other words the strict preference for leniency is the interior dominance region $\theta<1$, commonly written $[0,1)$, and with the conventional tie-break it is the whole set of imperfectly truthful firms.  The preference for leniency is strongest for the least truthful types and is monotone eroded as $\theta$ rises, disappearing only at the perfect truthfulness limit $\theta=1$ where $x(1-\theta)$ is identically zero. ∎

The auditor-contingent part of expected payment is $L(\theta,x)=x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)$ and $C(\theta,x)=t(\theta)+L(\theta,x)$ with $t$ $x$-free. On the binary support

$C(\theta,0)=t(\theta),\; C(\theta,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)$,

$\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta,1)-C(\theta,0)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)\ge0$,
$\Delta(\theta)=0\iff\theta=1$, $p(1)>0,\,F>0$.

Hence $C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)$ iff $\theta<1$, $C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1)$.  
$x^{*}=0$ is the unique strict minimiser for every imperfect type and $x^{*}(1)$ is indifferent.

Put $w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0$ on $\theta<1$, $g(x)=xp(x)$. Mod $t$,
$C(\theta,x)-t(\theta)=w(\theta)g(x)$. $1-\theta$ and $F$ are decreasing so
$w'(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0$ in the monotone sense, 
$\Delta(\theta)=p(1)w(\theta)$ is strictly decreasing, $\Delta(\theta)\downarrow0$ as $\theta\uparrow1$.

With the regular sign $p(x)+xp'(x)>0$,

$C_{x}(\theta,x)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)[p(x)+xp'(x)]>0$,
$C_{\theta x}(\theta,x)=[p(x)+xp'(x)]w'(\theta)<0$,

so $C$ has decreasing differences in $(\theta,x)$; the marginal cost of strictness $C_{x}$ is strictly decreasing in $\theta$ and the incremental cost
$\Delta(\theta)$ of $0\to1$ is strictly decreasing in $\theta$.

Best reply is flat on the interior:
$x^{*}(\theta)=0$ for $0\le\theta<1$, $x^{*}(1)\in\{0,1\}$, $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$.
The rent of leniency $G(\theta)=\Delta(\theta)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)>0$ is maximal for the least truthful types and is monotone eroded as $\theta$ rises, vanishing only at the perfect-truth limit.

Strict monotone comparative statics: $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\Rightarrow x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ never occurs on $]0,1[$. The strict monotone decreasing set for $x^{*}$ is empty; $x^{*}$ is weakly non-decreasing in $\theta$, in the penalty-only specification constant at the lenient corner.

Weak dominance: $C(\theta,0)\le C(\theta,1)$ on $[0,1]$ with strict inequality for $\theta<1$. Weak lenient dominance region is the whole imperfect interior $0\le\theta<1$, i.e. $\theta<1$. C(\theta_{2},x_{1})-C(\theta_{2},x_{0})
-\bigl[C(\theta_{1},x_{1})-C(\theta_{1},x_{0})\bigr]
 =\bigl[w(\theta_{2})-w(\theta_{1})\bigr]\bigl[g(x_{1})-g(x_{0})\bigr]<0,
\qquad\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},\;x_{1}>x_{0},
$$

so $x^{*}(\theta)$ is weakly non-decreasing in $\theta$,
$x^{*}(\theta_{2})\ge x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$,
and the conventional Spence–Mirrlees sorting is $x^{*}(\theta)\!\uparrow$
in $\theta$.  In strict monotone comparative statics

$$
\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\Longrightarrow x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})
$$

never occurs on $]0,1[$; the strict monotone decreasing set for $x^{*}$
is empty.

Weakly the lenient technology dominates the strict one on the whole
imperfect interior,

$$
C(\theta,0)\le C(\theta,1),\qquad 
C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\iff\theta<1,
$$

with the rent of leniency $G(\theta)=\Delta(\theta)=(1-\theta)p_{1}
F(\theta)>0$ maximal for the least truthful types and monotone eroded
to $0$ as $\theta\uparrow1$.  On the stated two–point support
$\Theta=\{0,1\}$ this is the strict preference $x^{*}(0)=0$ for the
malpractice type and the degenerate indifference $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at the
perfectly truthful type.  The usual applied statement is therefore the
weak dominance region $\theta<1$, i.e. $\;0\le\theta<1$, and in the
discrete parametrisation the strictly lenient type $\theta=0$.  Up to
the knife edge $\theta=1$, where ${\rm Pr}\{refusal\}=x(1-\theta)$
vanishes, the firm stays with the lenient corner and never moves to a
strictly more lenient auditor as $\theta$ rises. ∎

4.text:
The $x$-free tax can be dropped.  With refusal probability $x(1-\theta)$

$$
L(\theta ,x)={\rm Pr}\{refusal\}\,{\rm Pr}\{RS\mid refusal\}\,F(\theta)
        =x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)\ge 0,
\qquad 
C(\theta ,x)=t(\theta)+L(\theta ,x),
$$

so that on the binary admissible set

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta),
$$

$$
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)
      =p_{1}w(\theta)\ge 0,
\qquad w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0,
$$

$p_{1}=p(1)>0$, $F(\theta)>0$.  Hence

$$
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)\iff w(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,
\qquad C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1),
$$

i.e. $x=0$ is the unique strict minimiser of $C(\theta,\cdot)$ for every
imperfectly truthful type and $x^{*}(1)$ is indifferent.  Mod $t$,

$$
C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)=w(\theta)g(x),\qquad g(x)=xp(x),
$$

and $1-\theta$ and $F$ are decreasing, so in the monotone sense
$w'(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0$ on the interior and

$$
\Delta'(\theta)=p_{1}w'(\theta)<0,\qquad0<\theta<1,
$$

with $\Delta(\theta)\downarrow0$ as $\theta\uparrow1$.  In the regular
case $p(x)+xp'(x)>0$

$$
C_{x}(\theta ,x)=w(\theta)[p(x)+xp'(x)]>0,\qquad
C_{\theta x}(\theta ,x)=[p(x)+xp'(x)]w'(\theta)<0,
$$

so $C$ has decreasing differences in $(\theta ,x)$; the marginal cost
of strictness $C_{x}=w(\theta)[p+xp']$ is strictly decreasing in $\theta$
and the incremental cost of going from $x_{0}$ to $x_{1}>x_{0}$,

$$
C(\theta ,x_{1})-C(\theta ,x_{0})=[w(\theta)][g(x_{1})-g(x_{0})],
$$

is strictly decreasing in $\theta$.  Hence

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0\qquad0\le\theta<1,
$$

and $x^{*}(1)\in\{0,1\}$ with $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$.  Up to the degenerate
indifference at the top the best reply is the flat map
$x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$.

In particular

$$
C(\theta_{2},x_{1})-C(\theta_{2},x_{0})
-\big[C(\theta_{1},x_{1})-C(\theta_{1},x_{0})\big]
 =\big[w(\theta_{2})-w(\theta_{1})\big]\big[g(x_{1})-g(x_{0})\big]<0
$$

for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},\,x_{1}>x_{0}$; a higher $\theta$ makes a
strict auditor relatively cheaper, $C_{\theta x}<0$, the usual
Spence-Mirrlees ordering is $x^{*}(\theta)$ weakly non-decreasing in
$\theta$ and in the present penalty-only specification it is constant
at the lenient corner on the interior.

Hence in the strict monotone comparative-static sense

$$
\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\Longrightarrow x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})
$$

never occurs on $]\!0,1\![$; the strict monotone decreasing set for
$x^{*}(\cdot)$ is empty.  Weakly the lenient auditor dominates the
strict one on the whole interior,

$$
C(\theta,0)\le C(\theta,1),\qquad C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\iff\theta<1,
$$

i.e. the weak lenient dominance region is $0\le\theta<1$, commonly
written $\theta<1$.  On the stated two-point support $\Theta=\{0,1\}$
this is the strict preference $x^{*}(0)=0$ for the malpractice type
and the degenerate indifference $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at the perfectly
truthful type.  The rent of leniency
$G(\theta)=\Delta(\theta)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)>0$ is maximal for the
least truthful firms and is monotone eroded to zero at $\theta=1$ where
${\rm Pr}\{refusal\}=x(1-\theta)$ vanishes.  This is the reversal of the
naïve signalling story: more truthful firms are weakly less averse to
strictness, $x^{*}(\theta)\uparrow$ in the conventional sense, and the
present penalty-only model pools the whole imperfect interior at the
lenient corner. ∎

10.text:
Up to the $x$ free part $t(\theta)$

$$
L(\theta ,x)={\mathbb P}\{{\rm refusal}\}{\mathbb P}\{RS\mid{\rm refusal}\}
F(\theta)=x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)\ge 0,
\qquad C(\theta ,x)=t(\theta)+L(\theta ,x)
$$

so that on the admissible binary support

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta),
$$

and with $p_{1}=p(1)>0,\;F(\theta)>0$

$$
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)
      =p_{1}w(\theta)\ge 0,\qquad w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0,
$$

$$
\Delta(\theta)=0\iff\theta=1,\qquad
\Delta(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1 .
$$

Hence

$$
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)\iff \theta<1,\qquad C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1),
$$

i.e. $x=0$ is the unique strict minimiser of $C(\theta,\cdot)$ for every
imperfectly truthful type and the two technologies are payoff equivalent
only at the degenerate limit where ${\mathbb P}\{{\rm refusal}\}=x(1-\theta)$
vanishes.  Mod $t$,

$$
C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)=w(\theta)g(x),\qquad g(x)=xp(x),\qquad 
w'(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0,
$$

so that in the regular smooth notation

$$
C_{x}(\theta ,x)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)[p(x)+xp'(x)]>0,\qquad
C_{\theta x}(\theta ,x)=[p(x)+xp'(x)]w'(\theta)<0,
$$

$C$ has decreasing differences in $(\theta ,x)$.  The incremental cost
of strictness

$$
\Delta(\theta)=p_{1}(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0
$$

is strictly decreasing in truthfulness, $\Delta'(\theta)=p_{1}w'(\theta)<0$
on $]0,1[$, and $\Delta(\theta)\downarrow0$ as $\theta\uparrow1$.
The marginal cost of strictness $C_{x}=w(\theta)[p+xp']$ falls with
$\theta$.

In particular

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad0\le\theta<1,
$$

with $x^{*}(1)\in\{0,1\}$ and $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$.  Up to the trivial
indifference at the top the best reply is the flat corner
$x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$.  The rent of leniency

$$
G(\theta)=C(\theta,1)-C(\theta,0)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)>0
$$

is maximal for the least truthful types and is monotone eroded as
$\theta$ rises, vanishing only at $\theta=1$.

Hence in weak dominance terms the lenient auditor dominates the strict
one on the whole interior

$$
C(\theta,0)\le C(\theta,1),\qquad C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\iff\theta<1,
$$

i.e. the weak lenient dominance region is $0\le\theta<1$, conventionally
$\theta<1$.  On the stated two point support $\Theta=\{0,1\}$ this is the
strict preference $x^{*}(0)=0$ for the malpractice type and the degenerate
indifference $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at the perfectly truthful type.

In strict monotone comparative statics the best reply is weakly
non-decreasing, $x^{*}(\theta_{2})\ge x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ for
$\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$, and on the binary support it is in fact constant
on $[0,1)$. Consequently

$$
\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\Longrightarrow x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})
$$

never occurs on $]0,1[$; the strict monotone decreasing set for $x^{*}$
is empty.  The usual Spence–Mirrlees ordering is reversed,
$C_{\theta x}<0$, so the conventional sorting is $x^{*}(\theta)\!\uparrow$
in $\theta$.  Up to the degenerate indifference at $\theta=1$ the
penalty-only specification pools the whole interior at the lenient corner,
the advantage of leniency being monotone eroded to zero as
$\theta\to1$ where the refusal risk $x(1-\theta)$ disappears. ∎

16.text:
With the $x$ free part $t(\theta)$ deleted

$$
L(\theta ,x)=\Pr\{refusal\}\Pr\{RS\mid refusal\}F(\theta)
        =x(1-\theta )p(x)F(\theta)\ge0,\qquad 
C(\theta ,x)=t(\theta)+L(\theta ,x)
$$

and on the admissible binary support

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta),
$$

$$
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)
       =(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)=p_{1}w(\theta)\ge0 ,
\qquad w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0 ,
$$

$p_{1}=p(1)>0$, $F>0$.  Hence

$$
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)\iff w(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,
\qquad C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1),
$$

and $x=0$ is the unique strict minimiser of $C(\theta,\cdot)$ for every
imperfectly truthful type, $x^{*}(1)$ being indifferent.

Put $C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)=w(\theta)g(x)$ with $g(x)=xp(x)$.
$1-\theta$ and $F$ are decreasing, so in the monotone sense

$$
w(\theta_{2})<w(\theta_{1}),\qquad\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},
$$

and with the usual regularity $p+xp'>0$

$$
C_{x}(\theta ,x)=w(\theta)[p(x)+xp'(x)]>0,\qquad
C_{\theta x}(\theta ,x)=[p(x)+xp'(x)]w'(\theta)<0,
$$

i.e. $C$ has decreasing differences in $(\theta ,x)$.  The marginal
expected cost of strictness $C_{x}$ is strictly decreasing in $\theta$
and

$$
\Delta'(\theta)=p_{1}\big[-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)\big]<0,
\qquad0<\theta<1,
$$

so that the rent of leniency

$$
G(\theta)=\Delta(\theta)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)>0
$$

is strictly decreasing in truthfulness and $\Delta(\theta)\downarrow0$
as $\theta\uparrow1$.  Hence

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad0\le\theta<1,
$$

with $x^{*}(1)\in\{0,1\}$ and $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$.  In particular

$$
C(\theta_{2},x_{1})-C(\theta_{2},x_{0})-
\bigl[C(\theta_{1},x_{1})-C(\theta_{1},x_{0})\bigr]
 =\bigl[w(\theta_{2})-w(\theta_{1})\bigr]\bigl[g(x_{1})-g(x_{0})\bigr]<0
$$

for $x_{1}>x_{0}$ and $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$: a higher $\theta$ makes a
strict auditor relatively cheaper, $C_{\theta x}<0$, so the conventional
sorting is $x^{*}(\theta)\uparrow$ in $\theta$.

In strict monotone comparative statics there is therefore no interior
pair $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ with $x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$:
the strict monotone decreasing relation $x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$
for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ is empty on $]0,1[$ and the best reply is
flat at the lenient corner, $x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$.

Weakly the lenient auditor dominates the strict one,
$C(\theta,0)\le C(\theta,1)$ on $[0,1]$ with strict inequality
$C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)$ for the whole imperfect interior,
$0\le\theta<1$, i.e. $\theta<1$.  On the two point parametrisation
$\Theta=\{0,1\}$ this is the strict preference $x^{*}(0)=0$ for the
malpractice type and the degenerate indifference $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at the
perfectly truthful limit where $\Pr\{refusal\}=x(1-\theta)$ vanishes.
The preference for leniency is maximal at the least truthful types and
is monotone eroded to zero as $\theta\uparrow1$.  This is the usual
reversal of the naive signalling story: $x^{*}(\theta)$ is weakly
non-decreasing in $\theta$ and in the penalty-only specification it is
the constant pooling $x^{*}\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$ with indifference only at
$\theta=1$. ∎

15.text:
Up to the $x$ free tax the $x$ controllable part of expected payment is

$$
L(\theta ,x)=\Pr\{refusal\mid\theta ,x\}\,{\mathbb P}\{RS\mid refusal\}
F(\theta)=x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)\ge 0,
\qquad C(\theta ,x)=t(\theta)+L(\theta ,x),
$$

and on the admissible binary support

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta), 
$$

so that with $p_{1}=p(1)>0$, $F>0$,

$$
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)
=p_{1}w(\theta)\ge0,\qquad w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta),
$$

$$
\Delta(\theta)=0\iff\theta=1,\qquad 
\Delta(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1 .
$$

Hence

$$
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)\iff\theta<1,\qquad 
C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1),
$$

i.e. mod $t$ 

$$
C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)=w(\theta)g(x),\qquad g(x)=xp(x)\ge0,
$$

and $w(\theta)$ is strictly decreasing in the monotone sense,
$w(\theta_{2})<w(\theta_{1})$ for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$, so that

$$
C(\theta_{2},x_{1})-C(\theta_{2},x_{0})-
\bigl[C(\theta_{1},x_{1})-C(\theta_{1},x_{0})\bigr]
=\bigl[w(\theta_{2})-w(\theta_{1})\bigr]
\bigl[g(x_{1})-g(x_{0})\bigr]<0,
\qquad x_{1}>x_{0},\;\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},
$$

i.e. $C$ has decreasing differences in $(\theta ,x)$.  In the regular
smooth notation

$$
C_{x}(\theta ,x)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)\bigl[p(x)+xp'(x)\bigr]>0,
\qquad 
C_{\theta x}(\theta ,x)=\bigl[p(x)+xp'(x)\bigr]w'(\theta)<0,
$$

so the marginal expected cost of strictness $C_{x}$ is strictly
decreasing in $\theta$ and

$$
\Delta'(\theta)=p_{1}\bigl[-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)\bigr]<0,
\qquad 0<\theta<1,
$$

$$
\Delta(\theta)=p_{1}(1-\theta)F(\theta)\downarrow0,\qquad 
\Delta(\theta)\to0\;{\rm as}\;\theta\uparrow1 .
$$

Up to the inessential $t(\theta)$ the minimisation is $w(\theta)g(x)$.
Hence on the binary support

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad 
0\le\theta<1,
$$

and $x^{*}(1)\in\{0,1\}$ with $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$.  The best reply is the
flat corner $x^{*}\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$ and is weakly non-decreasing in
$\theta$,
$x^{*}(\theta_{2})\ge x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$,
the usual Spence–Mirrlees ordering being reversed, $C_{\theta x}<0$.
In particular the strict monotone relation

$$
\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\;\Longrightarrow\;x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})
$$

never holds on $]0,1[$; the strict monotone decreasing set for $x^{*}$
is empty.

Weakly the lenient auditor dominates the strict one,

$$
C(\theta ,0)\le C(\theta ,1),\qquad 
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)\iff\theta<1,
$$

with the rent of leniency
$G(\theta)=\Delta(\theta)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)>0$
strictly decreasing in truthfulness and vanishing only at the
perfect-truth limit where ${\mathbb P}\{refusal\}=x(1-\theta)\equiv0$.
The weak lenient dominance region is the whole interior
$0\le\theta<1$, conventionally written $\theta<1$.

On the stated two-point parametrisation $\Theta=\{0,1\}$ this is the
strict preference $x^{*}(0)=0$ for the malpractice type and the
degenerate indifference $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at the perfectly truthful type
$\theta=1$.  Up to the trivial tie at the top the lenient technology is
the unique strict best response for every imperfectly truthful type,
the advantage of leniency being largest for the least truthful firms and
being monotonically eroded to zero as $\theta\uparrow1$.  This is the
reversal of the naïve signalling story: a higher $\theta$ makes a strict
auditor relatively cheaper, $x^{*}(\theta)\uparrow$ in the conventional
sense, and the flat pooling $x^{*}\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$ is the penalty-only
limit. ∎

The level choice is unambiguous and does not need the differentiability or the sign of $p+xp'$ that is used for the strict monotone comparative static.

Up to the $x$-free tax $t(\theta)$

$$
C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)={\rm Pr}\{refusal\}{\rm Pr}\{RS\mid refusal\}F(\theta)
   =x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)=w(\theta)g(x)
$$

with $w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0$ on the interior and $g(x)=xp(x)\ge0$.
On the admissible binary support

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta),
$$

so that with $p_{1}=p(1)>0,\;F(\theta)>0$

$$
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)\ge0,
\qquad\Delta(\theta)=0\iff\theta=1 .
$$

Hence

$$
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)\iff\Delta(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,
\qquad C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1).
$$

The $x$-dependent part of expected payment is $w(\theta)g(x)$ with $w(\theta)$
the product of the two decreasing maps $1-\theta$ and $F$. In the monotone sense
$w(\theta_{2})<w(\theta_{1})$ for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ and

$$
\Delta(\theta_{2})-\Delta(\theta_{1})=p_{1}\big[w(\theta_{2})-w(\theta_{1})\big]<0,
\qquad\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},
$$

so the rent of leniency $G(\theta)=\Delta(\theta)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)$
is strictly positive on the whole interior, largest for the least truthful
types and monotone eroded as truthfulness rises, $G(\theta)\downarrow0$ as
$\theta\uparrow1$ where the refusal probability $x(1-\theta)$ vanishes.

Therefore

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,
\qquad0\le\theta<1,
$$

with $x^{*}(1)$ indifferent, $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$.  In level terms the lenient
technology is the unique strict minimiser for every imperfectly truthful type
and the two technologies are payoff equivalent only at the degenerate
perfect-truth limit.  The weak dominance $C(\theta,0)\le C(\theta,1)$ holds
on the whole interior $[0,1)$ with strict inequality for $\theta<1$.

On the stated discrete support $\Theta=\{0,1\}$ this is the strict preference
$x^{*}(0)=0$ for the malpractice type and the indifference
$C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at the top type. In the continuous description usually quoted
as $\theta<1$, i.e. $0\le\theta<1$, and the economic content is that the set
of types for which a firm actually chooses, and indeed strictly prefers, the
lenient auditor is the interior of the type space, the preference being
strongest at the malpractice end and being relaxed monotonically to the
knife-edge $\theta=1$ where the refusal risk disappears.

The sign of $C_{\theta x}$ and the strict monotone comparative static

$p(x)+xp'(x)>0$ and differentiability, the very regularity the problem
statement says is not guaranteed – $t,p,F$ are decreasing but not necessarily
differentiable and the implicit function theorem does not apply.  The level
choice $C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)$ for $\theta<1$ is a monotone comparison that
uses only the stated decreasing primitives and the explicit binary form of
$C$.  That is the set the question is asking for: the imperfect types, i.e.
$\theta<1$, on the binary support the malpractice type $\theta=0$ with the
degenerate indifference at $\theta=1$.

Put $C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)=w(\theta)g(x)$ with $g(x)=xp(x)$.
$1-\theta$ and $F$ are decreasing, so in the monotone sense

$$
w(\theta_{2})<w(\theta_{1}),\qquad\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},
$$

and with the usual regularity $p+xp'>0$

$$
C_{x}(\theta ,x)=w(\theta)[p(x)+xp'(x)]>0,\qquad
C_{\theta x}(\theta ,x)=[p(x)+xp'(x)]w'(\theta)<0,
$$

i.e. $C$ has decreasing differences in $(\theta ,x)$.  The marginal
expected cost of strictness $C_{x}$ is strictly decreasing in $\theta$
and

$$
\Delta'(\theta)=p_{1}\big[-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)\big]<0,
\qquad0<\theta<1,
$$

so that the rent of leniency

$$
G(\theta)=\Delta(\theta)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)>0
$$

is strictly decreasing in truthfulness and $\Delta(\theta)\downarrow0$
as $\theta\uparrow1$.  Hence

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad0\le\theta<1,
$$

with $x^{*}(1)\in\{0,1\}$ and $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$.  In particular

$$
C(\theta_{2},x_{1})-C(\theta_{2},x_{0})-
\bigl[C(\theta_{1},x_{1})-C(\theta_{1},x_{0})\bigr]
 =\bigl[w(\theta_{2})-w(\theta_{1})\bigr]\bigl[g(x_{1})-g(x_{0})\bigr]<0
$$

for $x_{1}>x_{0}$ and $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$: a higher $\theta$ makes a
strict auditor relatively cheaper, $C_{\theta x}<0$, so the conventional
sorting is $x^{*}(\theta)\uparrow$ in $\theta$.

In strict monotone comparative statics there is therefore no interior
pair $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ with $x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$:
the strict monotone decreasing relation $x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$
for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ is empty on $]0,1[$ and the best reply is
flat at the lenient corner, $x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$.

Weakly the lenient auditor dominates the strict one,
$C(\theta,0)\le C(\theta,1)$ on $[0,1]$ with strict inequality
$C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)$ for the whole imperfect interior,
$0\le\theta<1$, i.e. $\theta<1$.  On the two point parametrisation
$\Theta=\{0,1\}$ this is the strict preference $x^{*}(0)=0$ for the
malpractice type and the degenerate indifference $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at the
perfectly truthful limit where $\Pr\{refusal\}=x(1-\theta)$ vanishes.
The preference for leniency is maximal at the least truthful types and
is monotone eroded to zero as $\theta\uparrow1$.  This is the usual
reversal of the naive signalling story: $x^{*}(\theta)$ is weakly
non-decreasing in $\theta$ and in the penalty-only specification it is
the constant pooling $x^{*}\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$ with indifference only at
$\theta=1$. ∎

$$L(\theta ,x)= {\mathbb P}\{refusal\}{\mathbb P}\{RS\mid refusal\}F(\theta)
          =x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)\ge 0 ,\qquad 
C(\theta ,x)=t(\theta)+L(\theta ,x),$$

so on the admissible binary set

$$C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)$$

and with $p_{1}=p(1)>0,\;F(\theta)>0$

$$\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)
      =p_{1}w(\theta)\ge 0,\qquad w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0.$$

$$C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)\iff \Delta(\theta)>0\iff (1-\theta)F(\theta)>0
\iff\theta<1,\qquad C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1),$$

imperfectly truthful type and the two technologies are payoff equivalent
only at the degenerate limit where ${\mathbb P}\{refusal\}=x(1-\theta)$
vanishes.

Mod $t$,
$$C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)=w(\theta)g(x),\qquad g(x)=xp(x)\ge0,$$

$1-\theta$ and $F$. In the monotone sense $w(\theta_{2})<w(\theta_{1})$ for

$$\Delta(\theta_{2})-\Delta(\theta_{1})=p_{1}\big[w(\theta_{2})-w(\theta_{1})\big]<0,
\qquad\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},$$

so the rent of leniency
$$G(\theta)=C(\theta,1)-C(\theta,0)=(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta)>0$$
is strictly positive on the interior, largest for the least truthful firms
and monotone eroded as truthfulness rises, $\Delta(\theta)\downarrow0$ as
$\theta\uparrow1$.

Thus
$$x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad0\le\theta<1,$$
with $x^{*}(1)$ indifferent, $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$. In level terms the lenient
technology is the unique strict best reply for every non-perfect type.
The expected penalty saved by avoiding a refusal stays strictly positive for
all $\theta<1$ and is relaxed monotonically with $\theta$; a firm that
becomes more truthful never leaves the lenient corner, it stays with, and

In the weak dominance language this is the whole imperfect dominance
region
$$C(\theta,0)\le C(\theta,1),\qquad C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\iff\theta<1,$$
i.e. $0\le\theta<1$, conventionally written $\theta<1$. On the stated
discrete support $\Theta=\{0,1\}$ this is the strict best response
$x^{*}(0)=0$ for the malpractice type with the limiting indifference

perfect-truth boundary where the refusal risk $x(1-\theta)$ disappears.

robust to the non-differentiability of $t,p,F$ which rules out the

\Delta(\theta_{2})-\Delta(\theta_{1})=p_{1}\big[w(\theta_{2})-w(\theta_{1})\big]<0,
\qquad\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},
$$

i.e. the rent of leniency
$G(\theta)=\Delta(\theta)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)>0$
is strictly positive on the interior, maximal for the least truthful
types and monotone eroded to zero as $\theta\uparrow1$.
In regular notation $C_{x}>0$ and $C_{\theta x}=[p+xp']w'<0$, so $C$ has
decreasing differences and the marginal expected cost of strictness
$C_{x}=w(\theta)[p+xp']$ is strictly decreasing in $\theta$.

Therefore

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad0\le\theta<1,
$$

with $x^{*}(1)$ indifferent, $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$. Up to the degenerate
indifference at the top the best reply is the flat corner
$x^{*}\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$ and

$$
C(\theta ,0)\le C(\theta ,1),\qquad C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)\iff\theta<1,
$$

i.e. the lenient technology weakly dominates the strict one on the whole
imperfect interior and strictly dominates it for every non-perfect type.

That is the economically relevant choice set. The expected penalty saved
by avoiding a refusal stays strictly positive for every $\theta<1$ and
is relaxed monotonically with truthfulness, disappearing only at the
knife-edge $\theta=1$ where the refusal risk is identically zero.
A firm that becomes more truthful never leaves the lenient corner: it
continues to strictly prefer, and indeed keeps choosing, the more lenient
auditor $x=0$ for the whole interior $0\le\theta<1$, conventionally
written $\theta<1$. On the stated discrete support $\Theta=\{0,1\}$ this
is the strict best response $x^{*}(0)=0$ for the malpractice type with
the limiting indifference $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at $\theta=1$.

$\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ is a derivative pedantry about a discrete flat
best reply; what the question asks for is the level set on which leniency
is the cost-minimising choice, and that is the interior dominance region
$\Delta(\theta)>0$, i.e. $\theta<1$, effectively $\theta=0$ on the
two-point parametrisation, the advantage of leniency being strongest at
the malpractice end and being eroded monotonically to zero as
$\theta\to1$.

18.text:
Up to the $x$-free tax $t(\theta)$ the auditor controllable part of the
expected outlay is

$$
L(\theta ,x)={\mathbb P}\{{\rm refusal}\}{\mathbb P}\{RS\mid{\rm
refusal}\}F(\theta)=x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)\ge0 ,\qquad 
C(\theta ,x)=t(\theta)+L(\theta ,x) ,
$$

so that on the binary admissible set

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p(1)F(\theta) ,
$$

$$
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)
      =p_{1}w(\theta)\ge0,\qquad 
w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0,
$$

$p_{1}=p(1)>0$, $F(\theta)>0$.  Hence

$$
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)\iff w(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,
\qquad C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1),
$$

and mod $t$

$$
C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)=w(\theta)g(x),\qquad g(x)=xp(x)\ge0,
$$

so that in the monotone sense $w(\theta_{2})<w(\theta_{1})$ for
$\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ and

$$
C(\theta_{2},x_{1})-C(\theta_{2},x_{0})-
\bigl[C(\theta_{1},x_{1})-C(\theta_{1},x_{0})\bigr]
 =[w(\theta_{2})-w(\theta_{1})][g(x_{1})-g(x_{0})]<0,
\qquad x_{1}>x_{0},\;\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},
$$

i.e. $C$ has decreasing differences.  In regular notation
$C_{x}=w(\theta)[p+xp']>0$ and $C_{\theta x}=[p+xp']w'(\theta)<0$ with
$w'(\theta)=-F+(1-\theta)F'<0$, so the marginal expected cost of
strictness $C_{x}$ is strictly decreasing in $\theta$ and

$$
\Delta'(\theta)=p_{1}w'(\theta)<0,\qquad0<\theta<1,
\qquad\Delta(\theta)\downarrow0\;{\rm as}\;\theta\uparrow1 .
$$

Hence

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad0\le\theta<1,
\qquad x^{*}(1)\in\{0,1\},\;C(1,0)=C(1,1),
$$

up to the trivial indifference at the top the best reply is the flat
corner $x^{*}\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$ and

$$
C(\theta,0)\le C(\theta,1),\qquad 
C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\iff\theta<1,
$$

the rent of leniency $G(\theta)=\Delta(\theta)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)>0$
being maximal for the least truthful types and being monotone eroded to
zero as $\theta\uparrow1$ where ${\mathbb P}\{{\rm refusal}\}=x(1-\theta)$
vanishes.  In particular the conventional Spence–Mirrlees ordering is

$$
x^{*}(\theta_{2})\ge x^{*}(\theta_{1})\qquad\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},
$$

$ x^{*}(\theta)\uparrow$ in the usual sense, $C_{\theta x}<0$, and

$$
\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\Longrightarrow x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})
$$

never occurs on $]0,1[$.  The strict monotone decreasing set for
$x^{*}$ is therefore empty; the penalty-only specification pools the
whole imperfect interior at the lenient corner.

In level terms the lenient auditor is the unique strict minimiser for
every imperfectly truthful type.  The weak lenient dominance region is
the whole interior $0\le\theta<1$, conventionally written $\theta<1$, 
$C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)$ for $\theta<1$ and $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$.  On the
stated two–point support $\Theta=\{0,1\}$ this is the strict preference
$x^{*}(0)=0$ for the malpractice type and the degenerate indifference
$C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at the perfectly truthful limit.  Up to the inessential
indifference at $\theta=1$ the preference for leniency is strongest at
$\theta=0$ and is monotone eroded to zero as $\theta\to1$. ∎

17.text:
Up to the $x$ free tax $t(\theta)$

$$
L(\theta ,x)={\mathbb P}\{refusal\}{\mathbb P}\{RS\mid refusal\}F(\theta)
      =x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)\ge 0 ,\qquad 
C(\theta ,x)=t(\theta)+L(\theta ,x)
$$

and on the binary admissible set

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta),\qquad p_{1}=p(1)>0 .
$$

Modulo $t$

$$
C(\theta ,x)-t(\theta)=w(\theta)g(x),\qquad 
w(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0,\;g(x)=xp(x)\ge0,
$$

so that with $F>0$ decreasing and $1-\theta$ decreasing

$$
\Delta(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)
       =p_{1}w(\theta)=p_{1}(1-\theta)F(\theta)\ge0,
$$

$$
\Delta(\theta)=0\iff\theta=1,\qquad 
\Delta(\theta)>0\iff w(\theta)>0\iff\theta<1,
$$

and $w(\theta_{2})<w(\theta_{1})$ for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$ on the
interior.  In the regular smooth case $p+xp'>0$

$$
C_{x}(\theta ,x)=w(\theta)[p(x)+xp'(x)]>0,\qquad 
C_{\theta x}(\theta ,x)=[p(x)+xp'(x)]w'(\theta)<0,
$$

i.e. $C$ has decreasing differences in $(\theta ,x)$ and the marginal
cost of strictness $C_{x}=w(\theta)[p+xp']$ is strictly decreasing in
$\theta$.

Hence on the interior

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad 0\le\theta<1,
\qquad 
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1)\iff\theta<1,
$$

with $C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1)$ and $x^{*}(1)$ indifferent.  Up to the trivial
indifference at the top the best reply is the flat corner
$x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$ and the rent of leniency

$$
G(\theta)=C(\theta,1)-C(\theta,0)=(1-\theta)p_{1}F(\theta)>0
$$

is strictly decreasing in truthfulness and $G(\theta)\downarrow0$ as
$\theta\uparrow1$ where the refusal risk $x(1-\theta)$ vanishes.

$$
C(\theta_{2},x_{1})-C(\theta_{2},x_{0})
-\bigl[C(\theta_{1},x_{1})-C(\theta_{1},x_{0})\bigr]
 =\bigl[w(\theta_{2})-w(\theta_{1})\bigr]\bigl[g(x_{1})-g(x_{0})\bigr]<0,
$$

$x_{1}>x_{0},\;\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$, so $x^{*}(\theta)$ is weakly
non-decreasing in the conventional Spence-Mirrlees sense,
$x^{*}(\theta_{2})\ge x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$, and
on the binary support it is the constant pooling $x^{*}\equiv0$ on
$[0,1)$.  In the strict monotone comparative static sense

$$
\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}\Longrightarrow x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})
$$

never occurs on $]0,1[$; the strict monotone decreasing set for
$x^{*}(\cdot)$ is empty.  Weakly the lenient auditor dominates the
strict one,

$$
C(\theta,0)\le C(\theta,1),\qquad C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1)\iff\theta<1,
$$

i.e. the strict preference for, and indeed the unique strict minimiser,
$x=0$ is the whole imperfect interior $0\le\theta<1$, conventionally
written $\theta<1$.  On the stated two-point support
$\Theta=\{0,1\}$ this is the strict best response $x^{*}(0)=0$ for the
malpractice type and the degenerate indifference $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ at the
perfectly truthful limit $\theta=1$.  The advantage of leniency is

$$
